summary: The centered-capacity induction correctly proves central dominance: the pair-sum correspondence preserves the allowed lattices, circulation constraints, and even weighted degrees, and the quadratic comparison handles zero counts. Row completion, rank, degree-product bounds, reflected-fiber identification, odd-count rounding, and generic attainment of the minimum reflected cap count are valid. The canonical probability normalization and every hypothesis of accepted fact ebb695e93a721952 match its use, yielding the weighted bound for all containing closed halfspaces. Empty graphs, isolated vertices, empty zero-coordinate sets, and boundary atoms are covered. Exact exhaustive checks of 526 small ternary multigraphs, 4914 reflected roots, and 1576 admissible weighted-capacity instances found no counterexample. No mathematical errors or gaps were found.
